mainTopic: How גוים acquire slaves, and when captured or abandoned slaves go free
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא: a גוי cannot own a Jew's body, and גוים cannot own each other's body, but they can own each other's labor. The גמרא proves this by a קל וחומר, and רב פפא shows from סיחון's conquest of עמון and מואב that a גוי can also gain ownership by capture. A פסוק shows that a גוי can capture a Jew too. Next, רבי יוחנן rules that a slave who escapes captivity goes free. The גמרא asks how this fits with his ruling like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and answers according to אביי (before or after יאוש) and according to רבא (חזקיה's worry does not apply to one who escapes). Stories follow about the captured maidservants of שמואל and רבי אבא בר זוטרא, including שמואל's rule that a slave whose master gives up ownership goes free without a גט שחרור. Finally, a maidservant in פומבדיתא raises the question of freeing a slave to stop a sin. אביי and רבינא discuss it, and the challenge to אביי continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Gentiles cannot acquire you or each other
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying that גוים cannot acquire a Jew, and cannot acquire one another.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they cannot acquire from you, and they cannot acquire from one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא that learns from a פסוק about buying slaves from the nations. It now says what גוים cannot do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier part of the ברייתא said that a Jew may acquire slaves from the nations. This last part adds two limits: a גוי cannot acquire a Jew, and one גוי cannot acquire another גוי. The rest of this section will explain what those limits really mean.

keyTerms.meaning: from you, meaning from the Jewish people

phrases.english: but they cannot acquire from you,
phrases.notes: "They" are the גוים. A גוי cannot own a Jew as a full slave.

phrases.english: and they cannot acquire one from another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ברייתא that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גוים cannot acquire a Jew, and cannot acquire one another.

steps.title: The ברייתא starts to ask whether gentiles cannot acquire each other
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא appears to begin a new question: maybe גוים cannot acquire each other at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think that they cannot acquire one another?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא opens with "יכול", which usually brings up a possible mistaken idea. This line sets up the next move, where the גמרא will notice a problem with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An opening of "יכול" usually means the speaker is about to reject the idea. But the ברייתא just finished saying that גוים do not acquire each other. So it looks like it is rejecting its own rule.

keyTerms.meaning: one might have thought; brings up an idea that will be rejected

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לֹא יִקְנוּ זֶה אֶת זֶה?
phrases.english: One might think that they cannot acquire one another?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יִקְנוּ זֶה אֶת זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possibility about the rule that was just stated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is it true that גוים cannot acquire one another at all?

steps.title: But the ברייתא just said they cannot acquire each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: how can the ברייתא suggest rejecting the idea that גוים cannot acquire each other, when it just said they cannot?
steps.simpleTranslation: Can it be that one might think they cannot acquire one another? But you just said: they cannot acquire one another!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the "יכול" line with surprise. The ברייתא seems to contradict itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said plainly that גוים do not acquire each other. Then it opens with "יכול" as if that same idea were a mistake. Both cannot be right unless they are talking about two different kinds of ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: but you said! (pointing out a contradiction)

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לֹא יִקְנוּ זֶה אֶת זֶה?!
phrases.english: One might think that they cannot acquire one another?!

phrases.aramaic: הָאָמְרַתְּ: לֹא הֵם קוֹנִים זֶה מִזֶּה!
phrases.english: But you said: they cannot acquire one from another!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that step 2 seems to go against step 1.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא cannot treat "they don't acquire each other" as both the rule and a mistaken idea.

steps.title: They cannot acquire each other's body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא meant גוים cannot acquire each other's actual body.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: they cannot acquire one another for the body itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the problem by adding one word to the rule. The ban is only on owning the body of the person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two kinds of ownership: owning the person himself, and owning his work. The rule only says גוים cannot own each other's body. That leaves room for the "יכול" question to be about owning work.

keyTerms.meaning: for his body, owning the person himself

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as "גוים can never own slaves." The ban is only on owning the body; owning a person's labor is a different question.

phrases.english: This is what it means:

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הֵם קוֹנִים זֶה מִזֶּה לְגוּפוֹ.
phrases.english: and they cannot acquire one from another for his body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the rule to one kind of ownership
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule meant גוים cannot acquire each other in any way.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule only means they cannot own each other's body.

steps.title: Maybe they cannot acquire each other's labor either
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא now asks the question properly: maybe גוים cannot even own each other's work?
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think they cannot acquire one another even for his labor?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא restates its question, now clearly about owning a person's work. It sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since owning the body is ruled out, the open question is about owning work. The "יכול" suggests that the idea of "no ownership of work either" will be rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: the work of his hands, his labor

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לֹא יִקְנוּ זֶה אֶת זֶה
phrases.english: One might think they cannot acquire one another
for his labor?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יִקְנוּ זֶה אֶת זֶה לְמַעֲשֵׂה יָדָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the body/labor split from step 4 to ask the real question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can a גוי acquire another גוי's labor?

steps.title: A קל וחומר: a גוי can acquire another גוי's labor
steps.stepSummary: If a גוי can own a Jew's labor, he can surely own another גוי's labor.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say a קל וחומר: a גוי acquires a Jew; a גוי acquiring a גוי, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with a קל וחומר. A גוי can own a Jew's work, so he can surely own another גוי's work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה allows a Jew to be sold to a גוי for his work. A Jew is harder to own than a גוי, so if that works, owning a גוי's work must work too. So a גוי can acquire another גוי for labor, just not for the body.

keyTerms.meaning: a reasoning from a weaker case to a stronger one
is it not all the more so?

steps.whatToRemember: גוים cannot own each other's body, but they can own each other's labor. This is learned by a קל וחומר from a גוי owning a Jew's labor.

phrases.english: You can say a קל וחומר:
a גוי acquires a Jew;
phrases.notes: He means for the Jew's labor, as in ויקרא 25:47.

phrases.english: a גוי acquiring a גוי, is it not all the more so?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גוי can acquire another גוי's labor, by קל וחומר from a גוי acquiring a Jew's labor.

steps.title: Maybe this only works with money, not by taking hold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: maybe a גוי can only acquire another גוי by paying money, but not by taking hold of him, like capturing him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: this applies only with money, but by taking hold, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on how far the קל וחומר goes. Maybe it only proves ownership by money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of a Jew sold to a גוי is a sale, done with money. So the קל וחומר might only teach that money works. Taking hold of a person, like capturing him, might not work at all.

keyTerms.meaning: taking hold, gaining ownership by an act of control

phrases.english: But say: this applies only with money,
but by taking hold, no!
phrases.notes: Here "taking hold" means capturing a person, like in a war.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits what the קל וחומר of step 6 can prove.
steps.kashyaTarget: The scope of the קל וחומר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source case is a sale with money, so the proof may not cover gaining ownership by capture.

steps.title: רב פפא: עמון and מואב became permitted through סיחון
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא shows that a גוי can gain ownership by conquest: the land of עמון and מואב became סיחון's when he conquered it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: עמון and מואב became permitted through סיחון.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that taking hold does work for a גוי. He brings the case of סיחון conquering land from עמון and מואב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Israel was not allowed to take the land of עמון and מואב. But after סיחון conquered part of it, that part counted as his, so Israel could take it from him. This shows a גוי truly gains ownership by conquest, and the same applies to capturing a person.

keyTerms.meaning: two nations whose land Israel was told not to take
became pure, here meaning became permitted for Israel
the king of the אמורי who conquered land from them

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up conquest as a real way for a גוי to gain ownership, which the next step uses for a גוי and a Jew.

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
עמון and מואב became pure through סיחון.
phrases.notes: "Pure" means the land became allowed for Israel, because once סיחון conquered it, it was his land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: עַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב טָהֲרוּ בְּסִיחוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גוי can only acquire another גוי with money.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גוי also gains ownership of another גוי by conquest.

steps.title: What about a גוי taking hold of a Jew?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: we found that a גוי acquires a גוי by conquest; where do we learn that a גוי acquires a Jew that way?
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a גוי with a גוי; a גוי with a Jew, from where do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source that conquest works for a גוי over a Jew too. It sets up the פסוק that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סיחון's case was one גוי against other גוים. A Jew is harder to acquire, so it does not follow on its own that capture works on a Jew. The גמרא needs a separate source.

phrases.english: We have found a גוי with a גוי;
a גוי with a Jew, from where do we know?
phrases.notes: He means acquiring by capture, the kind of taking hold talked about in step 7.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן גּוֹי – גּוֹי; גּוֹי – יִשְׂרָאֵל, מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the result of step 8 to a new case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that a גוי gains hold of a Jew by capture.

steps.title: The פסוק: he took captives from them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק where a כנעני king captured some of Israel, showing a גוי can gain hold of a Jew by capture.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And he took captives from them."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. A גוי king fought Israel and took captives, so capture works on a Jew too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes the כנעני king of ערד taking Jewish captives in war. The תורה calls it real captivity, which shows a גוי can take hold of a Jew this way. That closes the gap left by סיחון's case.
steps.whatToRemember: A גוי can acquire another גוי's labor by money (קל וחומר) and by conquest (סיחון). A גוי can also take hold of a Jew by capture (במדבר 21:1).

phrases.english: As it is written: "And he took captives from them."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק "וישב ממנו שבי" shows that a גוי gains hold of a Jew by capture in war.

steps.title: A slave who escapes from prison goes free
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that a slave who escapes from captivity becomes free, and his master is forced to write him a גט שחרור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמן בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a slave who ran away from prison goes free. Not only that, his master is forced to write him a document of freedom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבי יוחנן about a slave who escaped from captivity. This ruling sets up the contradiction that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the slave escapes, he does not go back to his old master; he is free. The master must also write a גט שחרור so that the slave's freedom is complete and official.

keyTerms.meaning: He goes out to freedom; he becomes free
A document that frees a slave

phrases.english: Rav Shemen bar Abba said
Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
A slave who escaped from prison
goes free,
and not only that, but
his master is forced
to write him a bill of freedom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, moving from how a גוי acquires through capture to what happens when a captured slave escapes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave who escapes from captivity goes free, and his master is compelled to write him a גט שחרור.

steps.title: Contradiction from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: In the משנה, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says a redeemed captive slave stays a slave either way, and רבי יוחנן said the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in our משנה. This seems to contradict רבי יוחנן's ruling that the escaped slave goes free.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that either way he stays a slave. And רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: wherever רבן שמעון בן גמליאל taught something in our משנה, the הלכה follows him, except for the cases of the guarantor, צידן, and the last proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling with a different statement of רבי יוחנן himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that a captive slave goes back to his master even after he is redeemed. רבי יוחנן said the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and this case is not one of the three exceptions. So רבי יוחנן seems to say both "he goes free" and "he stays a slave."

keyTerms.meaning: He will be enslaved; he remains a slave
The final law follows his opinion

steps.confusionAlert: The three exceptions (guarantor, צידן, last proof) are cases from other places in ש"ס. They have nothing to do with slaves. They are listed only to show that our case is not an exception.

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: We learned: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
either way, he will be a slave;
phrases.notes: In our משנה this means a captive slave stays a slave, whether he was redeemed as a slave or as a free man.

phrases.english: and Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁשָּׁנָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בְּמִשְׁנָתֵנוּ –
phrases.english: Every place where Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel taught in our mishna,
the halakha follows him,
except for the guarantor and Tzaidan
and the last proof.
phrases.notes: These are three other משניות where the הלכה does not follow him. Our slave case is not on the list.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 11 by setting it against another ruling of the same אמורא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that an escaped slave goes free
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who says a captive slave stays a slave. So how can רבי יוחנן also say an escaped slave goes free?

steps.title: According to אביי there is no contradiction
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains the משנה as talking about a slave before the owner gave up hope (יאוש). רבי יוחנן's escaped slave is after יאוש, so the two rulings do not clash.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to אביי. He explains this one (the משנה) as before the owner gave up hope, and that one (רבי יוחנן's ruling) as after the owner gave up hope.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that one way of reading the משנה, אביי's, removes the contradiction. This also sets up the problem with רבא's reading in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before יאוש, the master still expects to get the slave back, so the slave stays his, as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says. After יאוש, the master has given up on him, so the escaped slave goes free, as רבי יוחנן says. The two rulings are about different situations.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well (for one opinion), usually followed by "but for the other..."
He sets it up as (explains the case as)
The owner's giving up hope of getting it back

phrases.english: Granted, according to Abaye,
he sets up this one as before despair,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the משנה with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

phrases.english: and that one as after despair.
phrases.notes: "That one" is רבי יוחנן's ruling about the slave who escaped from prison.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of Step 12, but only according to אביי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: before יאוש versus after יאוש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings seemed to talk about the same situation and to clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is before יאוש and רבי יוחנן's ruling is after יאוש, so they do not clash.

steps.title: According to רבא the contradiction remains
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the משנה as after יאוש. Then רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי יוחנן's escaped-slave ruling are about the same situation, and רבי יוחנן contradicts himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבא, who said the משנה is talking about after the owner gave up hope, there is a difficulty: רבי יוחנן contradicts רבי יוחנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the contradiction comes back if you read the משנה the way רבא does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the משנה's slave is after יאוש, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל still says he stays a slave. If רבי יוחנן rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, he should not free the escaped slave after יאוש, yet he does. The split by יאוש that worked for אביי does not help here.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יוחנן's words against רבי יוחנן's own words: a self-contradiction

steps.whatToRemember: Splitting the cases by יאוש solves the contradiction for אביי but not for רבא. The next step gives רבא's own answer.

phrases.english: But according to Rava,
who said it is after despair,
phrases.notes: "It" is the משנה with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

phrases.english: there is a difficulty: Rabbi Yoḥanan against Rabbi Yoḥanan!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer of Step 13 works only for אביי, so the challenge of Step 12 still stands for רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of רבי יוחנן's two rulings according to רבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבא, both cases are after יאוש. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, whom רבי יוחנן follows, keeps the slave enslaved, while רבי יוחנן frees the escaped slave.

steps.title: רבא explains why the escaped slave is different
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the contradiction in רבי יוחנן. A redeemed slave stays a slave because of חזקיה's worry. That worry does not apply to a slave who escapes, since he already risked his life.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא can tell you: Why does a redeemed slave stay a slave? Because of חזקיה's worry. An escaped slave is different. He just risked death to escape, so would he throw himself into the hands of enemy troops on purpose?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from Step 14. Both rulings can be after יאוש and still not clash, because each one has its own reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slave who is redeemed stays a slave only because of a worry: if redeeming freed slaves, they might let themselves be captured on purpose. A slave who escapes risked being killed to get out, so nobody suspects him of trying to be captured. The worry does not exist for him, so רבי יוחנן can free him.

keyTerms.meaning: One who escapes (here, a slave escaping captivity)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן is consistent. The redeemed slave stays a slave because of חזקיה's worry. The escaped slave goes free because that worry does not apply to him.

phrases.english: Rava can say to you:
What is the reason (a redeemed slave stays a slave)? Because of Chizkiya's concern;
phrases.notes: חזקיה worried that slaves would let themselves be captured, hoping to be redeemed and freed.

phrases.english: one who escapes is different:
now, he gave himself over to death (to escape),
would he throw himself into the hands of troops?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 14 according to רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reasons: the redeemed slave's rule rests on a worry that does not apply to an escaped slave.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since both cases are after יאוש, רבי יוחנן seems to contradict himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The redeemed slave stays a slave because of חזקיה's worry. The escaped slave goes free because nobody suspects him of seeking capture.

steps.title: שמואל's captured maidservant is redeemed and sent back
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's maidservant was captured. People redeemed her as a maidservant and sent her back. They told him she stays his under either view in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר שמואל's maidservant was taken captive. People redeemed her as a maidservant and sent her to him. They sent him a message: We hold like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, so she stays a maidservant either way. And even if you hold like the רבנן, we redeemed her as a maidservant, so she stays yours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case about this topic. This step sets up the next step, where the גמרא will show that the senders made a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the רבנן say a slave redeemed as a slave stays a slave, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he stays a slave either way. The senders said she was redeemed as a maidservant, so under both views she should go back to שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of being a maidservant (redeemed to stay a slave)
The Sages (the majority view in the משנה)

phrases.english: The maidservant of Master Shmuel was taken captive.
They redeemed her to be a maidservant,
and sent her to him.
They sent him a message:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנַן – כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סְבִירָא לַן,
phrases.english: We hold like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,

phrases.aramaic: אַתְּ – אִי נָמֵי כְּרַבָּנַן סְבִירָא לָךְ,
phrases.english: and you, even if you hold like the Rabbis,
we redeemed her to be a maidservant (for her).
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some leave it out. The meaning doesn't change.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the theory about redeemed slaves to a real case involving שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The redeemers assumed the maidservant stays שמואל's under both opinions in the משנה, because she was redeemed as a maidservant.

steps.title: The redeemers were wrong: it was after שמואל gave up hope
steps.stepSummary: The redeemers thought the redemption happened before שמואל gave up hope. In fact it was after יאוש, so שמואל did not keep her as a slave and did not even require a גט שחרור.
steps.simpleTranslation: They thought it was before שמואל gave up hope. That was not so. It was after he gave up hope. So שמואל certainly did not make her work as a slave, and he did not even require her to get a freedom document.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא corrects the senders' assumption and tells us what שמואל actually did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The senders' claim that she stays שמואל's rested on the idea that she was redeemed before יאוש, while he still hoped to get her back. In fact he had already given up hope, so in his view she was no longer his. She was fully free and did not even need a גט שחרור, as the next step explains.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner giving up hope of getting his property back
To make someone work as a slave

phrases.english: And they thought it was before (Shmuel's) giving up hope,
but it is not so. It was after giving up hope,
and Shmuel: it goes without saying
that he did not make her work as a slave,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא גִּיטָּא דְחֵירוּתָא נָמֵי לָא אַצְרְכָה.
phrases.english: but he did not even require her to get a document of freedom.

steps.confusionAlert: The key fact here is timing. The redeemers' argument only works before יאוש, and שמואל's maidservant was redeemed after he had already given up hope.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִינְהוּ סְבוּר – לִפְנֵי יֵאוּשׁ הֲוָה, וְלָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the redeemers' assumption from Step 16 and gives the true facts.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The redeemers' claim that the maidservant stays שמואל's.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: They assumed the case was before יאוש, but it was after יאוש, so the משנה's rules did not apply.

steps.title: שמואל's rule: a slave whose master gives up ownership goes free
steps.stepSummary: שמואל acted according to his known rule. A master who gives up ownership of his slave frees him with no need for a גט שחרור. He learns this from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל follows his own reasoning, because שמואל said: If someone gives up ownership of his slave, the slave goes free and does not need a freedom document. The פסוק says 'every slave of a man bought for money.' Does it mean only a male slave and not a female slave?! Rather, it means: a slave whose master has control over him is called a slave. A slave whose master has no control over him is not called a slave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that שמואל's behavior in the story matches a rule he taught elsewhere, and brings his source from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'slave of a man' cannot be coming to leave out a female slave, so שמואל reads them as 'a slave who belongs to a man,' meaning one who is under his master's control. Once the master gives up ownership (הפקר) or gives up hope (יאוש), the slave is not under anyone's control, so he is no longer a slave at all. That is why no גט שחרור is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: One who declares something ownerless (gives up ownership)
A document of freedom for a slave

steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, a slave is only a slave while his master has control over him. If the master gives up ownership or gives up hope, the slave is free without a גט שחרור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why שמואל did not require a גט שחרור for his captured maidservant after יאוש. In his view, the master's control is what makes someone a slave, and once that control is gone, so is the slavery.

phrases.english: Shmuel follows his own reasoning,
as Shmuel said:
One who gives up ownership of his slave, the slave goes free,
and does not need a document of freedom,
as it says: “And every slave of a man bought for money”:
Does it mean “a male slave” and not “a female slave”?!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עֶבֶד שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְרַבּוֹ עָלָיו –
phrases.english: Rather, a slave whose master has control over him
is called a slave;
one whose master has no control over him
is not called a slave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why שמואל did not require a גט שחרור in Step 17 by pointing to his general rule.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's behavior of not requiring a גט שחרור for his maidservant after יאוש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's own rule about הפקר of a slave, learned from שמות 12:44, 'עבד איש' meaning a slave under his master's control.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A master who gives up ownership of his slave frees him, and no גט שחרור is needed.

steps.title: רבי אבא בר זוטרא's maidservant is captured
steps.stepSummary: The maidservant of רבי אבא בר זוטרא was captured. A non-Jew redeemed her to marry her. The חכמים told her master to send her a גט שחרור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The maidservant of רבי אבא בר זוטרא was taken captive. A certain non-Jew from תרמוד redeemed her to be his wife. They sent a message to רבי אבא בר זוטרא: if you want to do the right thing, send her a bill of freedom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story about a captured maidservant. The חכמים advise her master to free her by sending a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the topic of captured slaves from the earlier steps. Here a non-Jew has redeemed her, not Jews, and he plans to marry her. The advice is surprising: the master should free her instead of trying to get her back.

keyTerms.meaning: a non-Jew from the city of תרמוד

phrases.aramaic: אַמְתֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זוּטְרָא אִישְׁתְּבַאי,
phrases.english: The maidservant of Rabbi Abba bar Zutra was taken captive.
A certain Tarmodite redeemed her to be his wife.
phrases.notes: A תרמודאה is a non-Jew from the city of תרמוד.

phrases.english: They sent a message to him himself:
If you want to act properly,
send her a bill of freedom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמְתֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זוּטְרָא אִישְׁתְּבַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story about a captured maidservant, following the story of שמואל's maidservant.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a non-Jew redeems a Jewish master's maidservant to marry her, the master should send her a גט שחרור.

steps.title: What would the bill of freedom accomplish?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the case is. If Jews can redeem her, there is no need for a גט. If they cannot, the גט seems useless.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If they are able to redeem her, why do we need a bill of freedom? If they are not able to redeem her, what will sending her a bill of freedom accomplish?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the advice by showing it seems pointless either way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a two-sided trap. If redemption is possible, they could simply redeem her as a slave without freeing her. If redemption is impossible, a piece of paper will not get her out of the non-Jew's hands.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? what are the circumstances?

phrases.english: What is the case?
If they are able to redeem her,
why do I need a bill of freedom?
If they are not able to redeem her,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי שַׁדַּר לַהּ גִּיטָּא דְחֵירוּתָא מַאי הָוֵי?
phrases.english: when he sends her a bill of freedom, what will it accomplish?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the usefulness of the advice in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The advice to send the maidservant a גט שחרור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both possible cases make the גט useless: either it is unnecessary or it has no effect.

steps.title: First answer: the community will join together to redeem her
steps.stepSummary: The case is where the Jews could redeem her. Once she is freed, they will join together and redeem her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the case is where they are able to redeem her. Once he sends her a bill of freedom, they will join together with one another and redeem her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks the first side of the question: redemption is possible. The גט is what will get people to act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The money for redeeming her exists, but people were not putting it together for someone who is only a maidservant. Once she is a free Jewish woman, the community will join together and redeem her. So the גט is not pointless; it is what moves the redemption forward.

keyTerms.meaning: really, actually (used to keep one side of a question)

phrases.english: Really, it is where they are able to redeem her;
and once he sends her a bill of freedom,
they will join together with one another,
and redeem her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 using its first side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case (redemption is possible) and shows the גט's practical effect.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If redemption was possible, the גט seemed unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גט is what gets the community to join together and redeem her.

steps.title: Second answer: the non-Jew will lose interest in her
steps.stepSummary: Or the case is where they cannot redeem her. Once the גט shows she was a slave, the non-Jew looks down on her and lets her be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: really, the case is where they are not able to redeem her. Once he sends her a bill of freedom, she becomes cheap in the non-Jew's eyes, and he lets her be redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer using the other side of the question: they cannot redeem her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גט works on the non-Jew, not on the Jews. It reveals that his intended wife was a Jew's slave, so he no longer values her. Then he releases her for a price they can pay.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you want, say (introduces a second answer)
she becomes cheap, looked down upon
in his eyes (literally, in his face)

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
Really, it is where they are not able to redeem her,
and once he sends her a bill of freedom,
she becomes cheap in his eyes,
phrases.notes: "His eyes" means the non-Jew who wanted to marry her. The גט shows him she was a slave.

phrases.english: and he lets her be redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the challenge of step 20, using its other side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case differently (redemption is impossible) and shows a different effect of the גט.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If redemption was impossible, the גט seemed useless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גט lowers her value in the non-Jew's eyes, so he releases her.

steps.title: Challenge: non-Jews value Jewish property highly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the second answer. A known saying states that non-Jews love Jews' animals more than their own wives, so learning she belonged to a Jew should not lower her in his eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't the Master say: the animals of Jews are more beloved to them than their own wives!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second answer from step 22 using a well-known saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second answer assumed the non-Jew would think less of her once he learned she was a Jew's slave. This saying suggests the opposite: non-Jews hold Jewish property in high regard. If so, the גט would not make him lose interest.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't the Master say? (introduces a challenge from a known teaching)

phrases.english: But didn't the Master say:
The animals of Jews are beloved to them,
more than their own wives!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the assumption behind the second answer in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that she would become cheap in the non-Jew's eyes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Non-Jews value what belongs to Jews even more than their own wives, so being a Jew's maidservant should not lower her.

steps.title: Answer: in private yes, in public it is shameful
steps.stepSummary: The saying is true only in private. In public, marrying a Jew's slave is considered shameful, so the non-Jew will give her up.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies only in private. But in public, the matter is considered degrading to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by limiting the saying to private matters, which saves the second answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Privately, a non-Jew may love what belongs to Jews. But a marriage is public, and openly taking a Jew's former slave as a wife would embarrass him. So the גט still makes him lose interest and release her.

keyTerms.meaning: the matter is degrading to them

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים told רבי אבא בר זוטרא to free his captured maidservant with a גט. Either it gets the community to redeem her, or it makes the non-Jew lose interest, because publicly marrying a Jew's slave is shameful.

phrases.english: These words apply in private,
but in public, the matter is degrading to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23 and keeps the second answer of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the saying: private vs. public.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Non-Jews always value Jewish property, so the גט would not lower her.
steps.terutzMaskana: In public it is shameful to marry a Jew's slave, so the גט does make the non-Jew give her up.

steps.title: A maidservant in פומבדיתא involved in forbidden behavior
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a story about a maidservant in פומבדיתא with whom people were committing forbidden acts.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain maidservant in פומבדיתא with whom people were doing forbidden acts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is opening a new story. This line only sets the scene for the rulings in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She was a שפחה, so she could not marry a Jew, and people were sinning with her. The question this raises is whether her master may free her so that the sin stops.

keyTerms.meaning: פומבדיתא, a major Jewish town and ישיבה center in בבל

phrases.english: There was a certain maidservant in Pumbedita,

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲווֹ קָא מְעַבְּדִי בַּהּ אִינָשֵׁי אִיסּוּרָא.
phrases.english: with whom people were doing forbidden acts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about freeing a slave, moving on from the discussion of a slave captured by non-Jews.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: a maidservant was the subject of ongoing forbidden behavior.

steps.title: אביי would force her master to free her except for שמואל's rule
steps.stepSummary: אביי says he would force the master to write her a גט שחרור, but he holds back because of רב יהודה's rule in the name of שמואל that freeing a slave violates a עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If not for what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, that anyone who frees his slave violates a positive commandment, I would force her master to write her a document of freedom.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי says what he would do in this case. He would force the master to free her, but he feels he cannot because of שמואל's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things pull in opposite directions here. Freeing her would stop the sin, but שמואל says freeing a slave breaks a עשה. אביי treats שמואל's rule as stronger, so he does not act.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָאו דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: If not for what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
anyone who frees his slave violates a positive commandment;
I would have forced her master,
and he would write her a document of freedom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָאו דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives אביי's ruling on the case described in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Freeing a slave violates a עשה, so אביי will not force the master to free her even to stop the sin.

steps.title: רבינא: רב יהודה agrees when there is a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says that in a case like this, where people are sinning, even רב יהודה would agree that the slave may be freed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: In a case like this, רב יהודה agrees, because of the forbidden matter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא disagrees with אביי's reading of רב יהודה. He says that when freeing her stops a sin, רב יהודה would allow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא keeps שמואל's rule as the general law but makes an exception. When there is an איסור at stake, preventing the sin comes before the עשה of keeping a slave. So according to רבינא, אביי's worry was not needed.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
In a case like this, Rav Yehuda agrees,
because of the forbidden matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with אביי's assumption that שמואל's rule applies even where there is a sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule against freeing a slave has an exception: it may be done to stop an איסור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main question for the rest of the discussion: whether stopping a sin allows freeing a slave.

steps.title: Does אביי really not allow freeing a slave because of a prohibition?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: does he really hold that a prohibition is not a reason to free a slave? It begins quoting a story, from רב חנינא בר רב קטינא in the name of רבי יצחק, about a woman who was half maidservant and half free.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does אביי hold that one may not free a slave because of a prohibition? But רב חנינא בר רב קטינא said in the name of רבי יצחק: There was an incident with a woman who was half maidservant and half free,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised at אביי's position and starts bringing a source against it. The story continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said he would not force the master because of the עשה. The גמרא is about to show from a known story that the master was forced to free a slave because of an איסור. If that is true, it seems to contradict אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't (he) say? This introduces a source used as a challenge
An incident, a story that happened
Half maidservant and half free woman

steps.confusionAlert: The quote is not finished here. The proof only becomes clear once the rest of the story, in the next lines, shows what was done for her.

phrases.english: And Abaye: because of a prohibition, he would not?!

phrases.aramaic: הָאָמַר רַב חֲנִינָא בַּר רַב קַטִּינָא
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Chanina bar Rav Ketina say
in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak:
There was an incident with one woman
who was half maidservant and half free,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to אביי's position from step 26 and challenges it with an earlier source.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's position that he would not force a master to free a slave, even to stop a sin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known story, told by רבי יצחק, seems to show that a master was forced to free a slave because of an איסור. That contradicts אביי's hesitation.
